rows.stem: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of events of sexual reproduction in a flower ?
rows.solution:
Pollen must first reach the stigma (pollination). The male germ cell then fuses with the female germ cell in the ovule (fertilisation), forming the zygote, which divides to form the embryo within the ovule. The ovule then develops a tough coat and is gradually converted into the seed. So the embryo is formed before the seed, not after it.

This is option (D) Pollination, Fertilization, Embryo, Seed.

rows.stem: The sexually transmitted disease caused by bacteria is :
rows.solution:
Gonorrhoea and syphilis are sexually transmitted diseases caused by bacteria. AIDS (caused by HIV) and warts are sexually transmitted diseases caused by viruses, and diarrhoea is not a sexually transmitted disease at all.

This is option (C) Gonorrhoea.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Arteries have valves as they have to withstand high pressure.

**Reason (R) :** Arteries are vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs.
rows.context: For Questions number 8 and 9, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Arteries carry blood under high pressure, but they do not have valves; they withstand the pressure because they have thick, elastic walls. Valves are found in veins, which carry blood at low pressure and need valves to keep it flowing in one direction. The Assertion is false.

Arteries are the vessels that carry blood away from the heart to the various organs of the body. The Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
What are hormones ? State any one function of the following hormones :

(i) Insulin

(ii) Adrenaline
rows.solution:
Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by the endocrine glands. They are released directly into the blood, which carries them to the parts of the body where they act, and they regulate various functions of the body.

(i) Insulin, secreted by the pancreas, regulates the blood sugar level.

(ii) Adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands, prepares the body to deal with stress or an emergency: the heart beats faster, so more oxygen is supplied to the muscles.

rows.stem:
Give reasons for the following :

(a) Herbivores have a longer small intestine.

(b) Inner lining of small intestine has numerous finger-like projections.

(c) Rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is much faster than that in terrestrial organisms.
rows.solution:
(a) Herbivores eat grass, which contains cellulose. Cellulose takes a long time to digest, so herbivores have a longer small intestine, which allows the cellulose to be digested.

(b) The finger-like projections are the villi. They greatly increase the surface area of the inner lining, so that the digested food is absorbed efficiently. The villi are richly supplied with blood vessels, which take the absorbed food to every cell of the body.

(c) The amount of oxygen dissolved in water is much lower than the amount of oxygen in air. So aquatic organisms have to breathe much faster than terrestrial organisms to obtain enough oxygen.

rows.stem: Which of the following compounds does *not* undergo addition reaction ?
rows.solution:
An addition reaction takes place only in an unsaturated compound, one with a carbon-carbon double or triple bond. \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) and \(\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}\) fit \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\), the alkenes (butene and pentene), and \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\) is ethyne, an alkyne, so all three undergo addition. \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\) (propane) fits \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\), a saturated alkane, which undergoes substitution, not addition.

The formulas \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) and \(\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}\) are read as alkenes, as in the textbook; each also has a saturated ring isomer, but the question does not intend those.

This is option (D) \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\).

rows.stem: Show the formation of \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) by transfer of electrons. Why does solid \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) not conduct electricity ? [Atomic number : Na = 11, Cl = 17]
rows.solution:
Sodium (2, 8, 1) has one electron in its outermost shell, and chlorine (2, 8, 7) needs one more to complete its octet. The sodium atom transfers its valence electron to the chlorine atom:

\(\mathrm{Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-}\) (2, 8, 1 to 2, 8: sodium cation)

\(\mathrm{Cl + e^- \rightarrow Cl^-}\) (2, 8, 7 to 2, 8, 8: chloride anion)

In the electron dot diagram, Na is drawn with one dot and Cl with seven crosses, and an arrow carries the dot to the Cl atom. The product is \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) and the chloride ion, \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\), drawn in brackets with a complete octet: \(\mathrm{(Na^+)(Cl^-)}\), that is \(\mathrm{NaCl}\).

Solid NaCl does not conduct electricity because its ions are held in a rigid structure and cannot move. Electricity is conducted only when the ions are free to move, as in molten NaCl or in its solution in water.

rows.stem:
Define the following terms :

(i) Corrosion

(ii) Rancidity

(iii) Exothermic reaction
rows.solution:
(i) Corrosion: the process in which a metal is attacked by substances around it, such as moisture, air and acids, so that it slowly gets eaten up. Rusting of iron is an example.

(ii) Rancidity: the oxidation of the fats and oils present in food, which changes the smell and taste of the food.

(iii) Exothermic reaction: a reaction in which heat (energy) is released along with the formation of the products. For example, burning of natural gas:

\(\mathrm{CH_4(g) + 2O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(g) + heat}\)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: Vision defect far-sightedness is found in the eye defects named as :
rows.solution:
A far-sighted person can see distant objects clearly but not nearby ones. This is hypermetropia. Presbyopia, the loss of the power of accommodation with age, also makes the near point recede, so nearby objects are hard to see while distant vision stays clear. Myopia is near-sightedness and a cataract is a clouding of the eye lens, so neither is far-sightedness.

This is option (C) Presbyopia and hypermetropia.

rows.stem: Draw the ray diagram showing refraction through a glass slab and write the relation between angle of incidence, angle of refraction and refractive index of glass.
rows.solution:
Ray diagram: draw a rectangular glass slab with air on both sides. Draw a ray falling obliquely on the top surface and the normal at the point of incidence. Inside the slab the ray bends towards the normal; at the lower surface it bends away from the normal and comes out into the air. The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways; show the incident ray produced as a dotted line to make this clear. Mark arrows on the rays and label the angle of incidence i and the angle of refraction r.

The relation is Snell's law: the refractive index of glass with respect to air is

\(n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}\)

rows.stem:
(a) State Ohm’s law and justify that \(V - I\) graph for Ohm’s law will always be a straight line passing through the origin.

(b) The figure shows \(V - I\) graphs for two identical wires A and B having the same length and area of cross-section, but made of different materials. Which of these wires will be more suitable for making the heating element of an electric heater and why ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (b) is decided by a printed graph: potential difference (V) on the vertical axis against electric current (I) on the horizontal axis, with two straight lines from the origin labelled A and B; which line is steeper is shown only in the drawing and is withheld here because it is the answer. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
(a) Ohm's law: the potential difference V across the ends of a metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current I flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same.

\(V \propto I\), so \(\dfrac{V}{I} = R\), a constant, and \(V = IR\).

Since R is the same for all corresponding values of V and I, the graph of V against I has the form \(y = mx\): a straight line with slope R. When I is 0, V is also 0, so the line passes through the origin.

(b) Wire B. The slope of a V-I graph gives the resistance. Line B is steeper, so B has the higher resistance; since both wires have the same length and area of cross-section, its material has the higher resistivity. The heat produced is \(H = I^2Rt\), so for the same current the wire of higher resistance produces more heat, and heating elements are made of materials of high resistivity. So wire B is more suitable for the heating element of the heater.

rows.stem:
A person was repairing an electric heater. He observed that there were three different connecting wires of three different colours in the cable attached to the heater.

(i) What are these three different wires called ? Name them colourwise.

(ii) What is the value of standard potential difference at which electricity is supplied in Indian homes for lighting ?

(iii) What is the role of (I) earthing and (II) fuse in domestic electric circuits ?
rows.solution:
(i) The three wires are:

1. Live wire (positive): red insulation.

2. Neutral wire (negative): black insulation.

3. Earth wire: green insulation.

(ii) Electricity is supplied to Indian homes at a potential difference of 220 V.

(iii) (I) Earthing: the earth wire is connected to a metal plate buried deep in the earth near the house and to the metallic body of the appliance. It provides a low-resistance conducting path for the current, so if current leaks to the metallic body, it flows to the earth and keeps the potential of the body equal to that of the earth. The user is protected from a severe electric shock.

(II) Fuse: a fuse is a safety device connected in series in the circuit. When an unduly high current flows because of overloading or a short circuit, the fuse wire heats up, melts and breaks the circuit, which prevents damage to the appliances and the circuit.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
(i) Write the name and statement of the rule used to determine the direction of the :

(I) force experienced by a straight current-carrying conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field.

(II) magnetic field produced around a straight conductor carrying electric current.

(ii) Two straight current-carrying conductors (A) and (B) are shown in the figures below :

(I) Mark the direction of the magnetic fields around these current-carrying conductors (A) and (B).

(II) Compare the strengths of magnetic fields produced (1) at points P and Q and (2) at points Q and R due to these current-carrying conductors, qualitatively.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (ii) depends on two printed drawings of vertical straight conductors, each passing through the centre O of horizontal circles: (A) carries I = 1 A with point P on a circle 2 cm from O; (B) carries I = 2 A with point Q on a circle 2 cm from O and point R on a circle 4 cm from O. The currents, the distances and the direction of each current are given only in the drawing; the current directions (arrowheads) decide (I) and are withheld here. Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
(i) (I) Fleming's left-hand rule. Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force acting on the conductor (its direction of motion).

(II) The right-hand thumb rule. Imagine holding the current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.

(ii) (I) By the right-hand thumb rule the field lines are concentric circles around each wire.

Conductor (A): the current of 1 A flows upwards, so the field lines run anticlockwise when seen from above. Mark the arrows on the circle through P in that sense.

Conductor (B): the current of 2 A flows downwards, so the field lines run clockwise when seen from above. Mark the arrows on both circles, through Q and through R, in that sense.

(II) The magnetic field of a straight conductor increases with the current and decreases as the distance from the wire increases.

(1) P and Q are both 2 cm from their wires, but the current in (B) is 2 A against 1 A in (A). So the magnetic field at Q is stronger than at P (about twice).

(2) Q and R lie around the same wire carrying 2 A, but R is 4 cm away and Q only 2 cm. So the magnetic field at Q is stronger than at R (about twice).
